title: Pirates Hijack Sanctioned Tanker Sibu 1 (Seamull) in Gulf of Aden, Steer Toward Somalia
detail: Six armed pirates in two skiffs boarded and seized the 32,200-dwt product tanker Sibu 1 — also tracked under its former name Seamull, and sanctioned by the US Treasury in December 2025 for carrying Iranian 'shadow fleet' petroleum products — approximately 136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla, Yemen, in the Gulf of Aden on Thursday, August 20, 2026. The vessel's AIS reportedly broadcast 'PIRATE ONBOARD HELP' before changing course toward Somalia's Puntland coast, joining Honour 25, Sward, Eureka, Asana, and Lutuf as the sixth commercial vessel seized by resurgent Somali pirates since April 2026. UKMTO and EU NAVFOR Atalanta are tracking the vessel; its claimed Eritrean registry is reportedly false. The Indian High Commission in Nairobi confirmed all 16 Indian nationals among the vessel's 20-member crew were safe, alongside crew of other nationalities. Analysts attributed the piracy surge to naval patrol forces stretched thin by the wider Red Sea/Iran conflict.

title: Puntland Demands Answers After Second Deadly Strike Hits Garmaal Fishing Community; FGS Promises Investigation
detail: A second airstrike or naval shelling struck the Garmaal coastal area of Dangorayo district, Nugaal region, Puntland, on Thursday, August 20, 2026 — two days after the August 18 strike near the same location that Puntland officials and this tracker initially reported as killing four suspected pirates. Puntland's regional government formally condemned both the August 18 and August 20 incidents, saying unidentified international warships or aircraft struck fishing boats and gear and endangered local livelihoods, and warned the strikes could undermine Puntland's counter-piracy cooperation with international partners. Family members and community elders disputed the initial 'suspected pirates' characterization of the four August 18 dead — named locally as Ahmed Ali Jama Dhahar, Heego Mohamed Ducaale, Waraad Yusuf Ubeed, and Caydarus Yusuf Ilmi — insisting they were ordinary fishermen returning from near where the hijacked cargo ship Lutuf was anchored. Puntland officials said Turkish surveillance aircraft had been observed patrolling the area, but Turkey neither confirmed nor denied involvement. Somali federal State Minister for Defense Omar Ali Abdi said on August 22-23 that Mogadishu was 'aware of military operations' off the Puntland coast, asserted federal authority over authorizing any such strikes, and promised 'a comprehensive report' once an assessment is complete, without identifying the responsible force. As of August 24, the strikes' authorization, the identity of the operating force, and verification of civilian harm remained unresolved, straining relations between Puntland and the Federal Government amid the wider piracy resurgence.
